source.author: verg
source.text: omnibus extemplo Teucris iubet ordine duci instratos ostro alipedes pictisque tapetis; aurea pectoribus demissa monilia pendent, tecti auro fulvum mandunt sub dentibus aurum; absenti Aeneae currunt geminosque iugalis semine ab aetherio, spirantis naribus ignem, illorum de gente, patri quos daedala Circe supposita de matre nothos furata creavit.
source.text_original: omnibus extemplo Teucris iubet ordine duci / instratos ostro alipedes pictisque tapetis; / aurea pectoribus demissa monilia pendent, / tecti auro fulvum mandunt sub dentibus aurum; / absenti Aeneae currunt geminosque iugalis / semine ab aetherio, spirantis naribus ignem, / illorum de gente, patri quos daedala Circe / supposita de matre nothos furata creavit.
source.text_english: At once he orders that for all the Teucrians, in rank, they be led out, horses draped with purple and with painted saddle-cloths; golden necklaces hang down over their chests, and covered with gold they chew the tawny gold beneath their teeth; for the absent Aeneas there come twin steeds, and from heavenly seed, breathing fire from their nostrils, of that same race, those whom the crafty Circe, by substituting a mother beneath them, had stolen away and created as bastards from their father’s stock.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: optimus hasta hic Peleus, hic ense furens agnoscitur Aeson; fert gravis invito victorem Nestora tergo Monychus, ardenti peragit Clanis Actora quercu; nigro Nessus equo fugit, acclinisque tapetis in mediis vacuo condit caput Hippasus auro.
reuse.text_original: optimus hasta / hic Peleus, hic ense furens agnoscitur Aeson; / fert gravis invito victorem Nestora tergo / Monychus, ardenti peragit Clanis Actora quercu; / nigro Nessus equo fugit, acclinisque tapetis / in mediis vacuo condit caput Hippasus auro.
reuse.text_english: Here Peleus is recognized as the best with the spear, here Aeson is raging with the sword; heavy Monychus carries Nestor, the victor, on his unwilling back, Clanis pursues Actora with a blazing oak; Nessus flees on a black horse, and Hippasus, leaning against the tapestries in the midst, buries his head in empty gold.
